correctness.rationale: PASS: The polar form of Q_B(X)=tr(BX^2) is tr((BX+XB)Y). Orthogonality over X gives the squared magnitude q^4 times a character sum on ker L_B, so supported magnitudes are q^(4-r_B/2). For odd fields trB=0 nonzero implies image span(I,B) of rank 2, singular trace-nonzero B gives rank 3, and invertible trace-nonzero B rank 4; counting the classes proves R_odd(q)=q^8-2q^7+q^6+2q^5-q^4-q^2+1. In characteristic 2, scalar B gives an additive square-phase with exactly A=lambda^(q/2)I; nonscalar B centralizer span(I,B) gives two independent trace constraints, hence R_even=q^6-q^3+q. Independent full integer Fourier-Walsh/cyclotomic checks for q=2 (256 frequency pairs, rank 58) and q=3 (6561 pairs, rank 3313) confirmed all zero/nonzero predictions and squared amplitudes. Arbitrary q is established by field-algebra proof, not the prime-field enumeration.
